Standing at {{height|cm=191}},{{Cite web |url=http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=BJG |title=Aaron Jackson altura: B {{!}} 1.93 m |work=ACB.com |language=es |access-date=2017-07-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105180436/http://www.acb.com/jugador.php?id=BJG |archive-date=2012-11-05 |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=JAC-AAR-86 |title=Aaron Lee Jackson Altezza: 193 cm . |access-date=2017-07-24 |language=it |archive-date=2017-10-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171005201618/http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=JAC-AAR-86 |url-status=dead }}[http://www.draftexpress.com/profile/Aaron-Jackson-5677/ AARON JACKSON HEIGHT: 6'3" (193 cm).] ,he plays at both the [[point guard]] and [[shooting guard]] positions, with point guard being his main position. He has played professionally in Europe and China, since finishing his [[college basketball|collegiate career]] with [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], earning plaudits for his play and achievements, most notably while with the Spanish club [[Bilbao Basket]] and the Russian club [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]. ==High school== Jackson attended and played high school basketball at [[Northwest Catholic High School]], in [[West Hartford, Connecticut|West Hartford]], [[Connecticut]], and at [[Worcester Academy]], in [[Worcester, Massachusetts|Worcester]], [[Massachusetts]]. He won two Connecticut state championships while at Northwest Catholic High School, and spent a year at Worcester Academy prep school, for his [[postgraduate year]]. While playing under [[head coach]] [[Mo Cassara]] at the second, he was recruited by [[NCAA Division I]] program [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], of the [[Atlantic 10 Conference]], in April 2005.[http://www.scout.com/story/371075-aaron-jackson-signs-national-letter-of-intent?s=143 "Aaron Jackson signs national letter of intent."], ''[[Scout.com]]'', Pittsburgh, 18 April 2005. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. ==College career== At the time when Jackson started his [[college basketball]] career at [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], the school's basketball program was in the midst of one of its worst stretches ever, reaching 10 wins just twice in 11 years, in repeating losing seasons. The 2005–06 season wouldn't reverse the trend, on the contrary as the 3–24 season was the worst in the school's [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball#Yearly results|92 year history]].Peretic, Joel. [http://www.pittsburghsportsreport.com/PSR/node/5067 "Hero, Healer, Leader."], ''Pittsburgh Sports Report (commercial website)'', 14 November 2012. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. Despite this, Jackson started 21 of 27 games, and had comparatively good stats for a freshman (second on the team in assists and steals, and third in assist-to-turnover ratio in the conference).[http://www.goduquesne.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/aaron_jackson_210275.html "Aaron Jackson"], ''[[Duquesne Dukes]]''. Retrieved on 27 March 2015. The team's head coach, [[Danny Nee]], was fired and replaced by [[Ron Everhart]], and he would make sweeping changes to the roster, bringing in 10 new players, whilst only keeping two from the previous team, including Jackson, after a face to face meeting between the two.{{cite news |author1=Phil Axelrod |title=Watch out for Aaron Jackson |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/98238818/watch-out-for-aaron-jackson/ |access-date=23 March 2022 |work=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |date=8 November 2006 |page=D4}} In a team shook by a campus shooting ([[#Duquesne shooting|see Duquesne shooting]]), Jackson was a leader for the team as a sophomore. Playing in all games – starting most – he was in the conference top-10 in assists (3.8 per game) and steals (1.4 per game), whilst adding 11 points and 5 rebounds on average, as part of a team with an improved collective 10–19 record. Jackson's junior season followed that trend, though he earned less minutes of playing time, as per Everhart's rotation policy. He led his team in minutes and assists, while also scoring in double figures and, posting 5+ rebounds 13 games during the season. With averages of 9 points per game and 4 rebounds per game, for the season. The Dukes had their first winning season since 1994. Fittingly, he reached the pinnacle of his collegiate career in his last college season. Being the only senior in a team with seven freshmen, he started in every single game, as he led the team in scoring and assists (with a school record of 194), and was second on the team in rebounding and steals. His stats also ranked in the top 5 for the whole conference, in seven different statistical categories (of which included scoring, assists, steals, and minutes), which led to him being selected to the [[2008–09 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season#Atlantic 10 Men.27s Basketball All-Conference Teams|All-A 10 first team]], and the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District 4 first team,[http://static.psbin.com/1/k/wkwc0xiiiavy2k/D1all-district09.pdf "National Association of Basketball Coaches Announces 2009 Division I All-District Teams."], ''[[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]]'', Kansas City (MO), 5 March 2009. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. also being awarded [[2008–09 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season#All-Conference Awards .5B9.5D.|A-10 Most Improved Player]]. On a team level, it was also successful season, as the Dukes had a 21–13 record in the regular season, their best since 1971, which allowed them to enter the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] tournament. Jackson played in his last Dukes game in the first round of the NIT, against [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], which was a befitting farewell, as he scored 46 points in the game (tied for the fourth highest single-game point total for the school), in a double [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090322203144/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290770259 "Combo of Vassallo and Allen help Hokies overcome Jackson's 46."], ''[[ESPN]]'', Blacksburg, 19 March 2009. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. At the end of his Duquesne college career, Jackson's name was inscribed into the university's record books, as his 194 assists in 2009, broke [[Norm Nixon]]'s previous school record. Besides that, he was also tied for 1st place in games played (having played in all of his team's games, in every season), was in 3rd place in career assists (with 505), was in 6th place in steals (169), and in 7th place in field goal percentage. ==Professional career== With his collegiate career over, Jackson turned his sights to the professional game and the [[2009 NBA draft]], first by playing in the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]]Waldrop, Melinda. [https://www.dailypress.com/2009/04/12/portsmouth-invitational-tournament-rise-follows-06-shooting/ "Portsmouth Invitational Tournament: Rise Follows '06 Shooting."], ''[[Daily Press (Virginia)]]'', Portsmouth (VA), 12 April 2009. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. then by attending workouts with a half-dozen NBA teams, despite this he was not predicted to be drafted though he did attract attention from the [[Indiana Pacers]].Mackall, Dave. [http://triblive.com/x/pittsburghtrib/sports/college/s_630642.html#axzz3ahrIg72B "Duquesne's Jackson making late draft push."], ''[[Pittsburgh Tribune-Review]]'', 23 June 2009. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. He would go [[undrafted]] in the end but did rejoin the Pacers for the [[NBA Summer League]] where, in a de facto competition with [[A. J. Price]] for the third point guard spot on the roster, Price was signed over him. Not financially interested in [[NBA Development League|D-League]] contract offers, Jackson planned a move abroad. ===Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi (2009–2010)=== Jackson moved to [[Antalya Büyükşehir Belediyesi]] of the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]] in July 2009, penning his first professional contract.[http://www.goduquesne.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/072909aaf.html "Aaron Jackson Signs With Antalya of the Turkish Basketball League"], ''[[Duquesne Dukes]]'', Pittsburgh, 29 July 2009. Retrieved on 27 March 2015. For his first experience abroad he suffered from culture shock but developed his game in what he described as a physical league with hard fought games and had a good season statistically with 15,2 points, 4,9 rebounds and 4 assists per game.[http://www.lavozdigital.es/cadiz/rc/20100930/deportes/baloncesto/aaron-jackson-bala-camino-201009301803.html "Aaron Jackson a bullet in his path."], ''LaVozDigital (commercial website)'', Madrid, 30 September 2010. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|es}} ===Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna (2010)=== Antalya finished in [[2009–10 Turkish Basketball League|mid-table]], missing the playoffs, but Jackson's season wasn't over as he then signed for Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]] side [[Virtus Pallacanestro Bologna|Virtus Bologna]] in April 2010 as a replacement for the injured [[Petteri Koponen]] to play in the playoffs.Conroy, Denny. [http://recruiting.scout.com/story/969657-ajax-signs-with-italian-team "Ajax signs with Italian team."], ''[[Scout.com]]'', 13 May 2010. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.Aquino, Luca. [http://corrieredibologna.corriere.it/bologna/notizie/basket_city/2010/30-aprile-2010/virtus-ha-scelto-aaron-jackson-1602935188630.shtml "Virtus has chosen Aaron Jackson."], ''[[RCS MediaGroup#Quotidiani .28Newspapers.29 Sector|Corriere di Bologna]]'', 30 April 2010. Retrieved on 27 March 2015.{{in lang|it}} He was an instant fit for the team, starting in all games of their first round [[2009–10 Lega Basket Serie A#Cant.C3.B9 .E2.80.93 Virtus Bologna|playoff run]], his good performances and statistics prompting the team to offer him an extension.[http://www.ilrestodelcarlino.it/bologna/sport/2010/06/15/345555-virtus_punto.shtml "Virtus, update."], ''[[Il Resto del Carlino]]'', 15 June 2010. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|it}} ===Bilbao Basket (2010–2012)=== It was to be in vain for Virtus as Jackson signed a contract with Spanish [[Liga ACB]] team [[Bilbao Basket]], signing a two-year deal (the second year an option) with an NBA clause in June 2010,[http://www.goduquesne.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/062210aaa.html "Aaron Jackson Agrees to Deal with Bilbao of the Spanish ACB."], ''[[Duquesne Dukes]]'', Pittsburgh, 22 June 2010. Retrieved on 21 May 2015. after a summer league appearance with the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] yielded no contract he joined the team for good.[http://bilbaobasket.elcorreo.com/noticias/2010-08-24/aaron-jackson-presentado-como-201008241406.html "Aaron Jackson, introduced as a new Bilbao Basket player."], ''[[El Correo]]'', 24 August 2010. Retrieved on 27 March 2015.{{in lang|es}} He was brought in by coach [[Fotios Katsikaris]] to replace the club's legend, [[Javi Salgado]], with a more athletic and dynamic play-maker, a decision that earned critics from fans and observers.[https://es.eurosport.yahoo.com/16082010/21/katsikaris-marca-objetivos-copa-play-off.html "Katsikaris targets the cup and the playoffs."], ''[[Eurosport]]'', Getxo, 16 August 2010. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|es}} A frosty reception awaited Jackson in Spain, having to adapt to the competition level, considered the best national domestic league in Europe, and his dual role as facilitator and crunch time scorer, he had ups and downs before becoming the focal point of his team, leading them to 6th in the league before having a decisive role in their run to the [[2011 ACB Playoffs|playoff]] final, beating powerhouse [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in the process.Borja Tovar [http://www.talkbasket.net/5737-basque-cinderella-bizkaia-bilbao-basket-shocks-the-acb-and-makes-it-to-the-finals.html "Basque cinderella BBB makes the ACB final in a shocker"], ''Talkbasket.net (Content website)'', 3 June 2011. Retrieved on 1 April 2015. Though they would lose in the final to [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|Barcelona]], Jackson played the most minutes of any player in the playoffs, also breaking the top 10 for scoring, rebounding, assists and steals[http://www.acb.com/stsindiv.php?cod_competicion=LACB&cod_edicion=55&cod_fase=PT "Individual statistics – Liga ACB 2010–11 (Playoffs)."], ''[[Liga ACB]]''. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|es}} and the option on his second year was taken by the Basques, with the guard motivated by the prospect of playing in the [[EuroLeague]], the continents' premier competition.[http://www.marca.com/2011/06/17/baloncesto/acb/1308319115.html "Aaron Jackson will stay another season in Bilbao."], ''[[Marca (newspaper)]]'', Bilbao, 17 June 2011. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|es}} His second season in Spain was as successful, being named the fifth best point guard in the Liga ACB[http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=84464 "Sergio Llull, best point guard of the 2011–2012 Liga Endesa."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509153216/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=84464 |date=May 9, 2012 }}, ''[[Liga ACB]]'', 4 May 2012. Retrieved on 21 May 2015.{{in lang|es}} as he led his team to another playoff appearance though this time they lost in the [[2012 ACB Playoffs#Caja Laboral vs. Gescrap Bizkaia|first round]], Jackson top scoring for Bilbao in both games. Above all he discovered the EuroLeague, among the European elite he had seesaw performances, none so evident in two back-to-back games against Real Madrid, the first a shocker with only 2 points in 20 minutes in a loss,[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=003413&seasoncode=E2011 "Jackson, Aaron: 2011–12 Statistics."], ''[[EuroLeague]]''. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. the second a Top 16 Week 4 MVP performance, scoring 15 points with 10 assists and only 1 turnover in a 93–69 victory that allowed Bilbao to finish above Madrid in their group and reach the [[2011–12 Euroleague Quarterfinals|Quarterfinals]].[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/93815/top-16-week-4-bwin-mvp-aaron-jackson-gescrap-bb "Top 16, Week 4 bwin MVP: Aaron Jackson, Gescrap BB."], ''[[EuroLeague]]'', 10 February 2012. Retrieved on 11 April 2015. In the playoffs, he upped his game against future finalist [[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]], leading Bilbao in points, assists and steals to rank fifth for the playoff phase in [[Performance Index Rating]],[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/98276/cska-adds-point-guard-jackson "CSKA adds point guard Jackson."], ''[[EuroLeague]]'', 19 June 2012. Retrieved on 21 May 2015. despite this Bilbao was overpowered by the Russians and lost the series 3–1. Jackson was out of contract at the end of the 2011–12 season and turned down a contract extension offer from Bilbao, ending his tenure there following "two marvelous years".{{cite news |url=http://bilbaobasket.elcorreo.com/noticias/2012-05-23/aaron-jackson-tambien-deja-201205231455.html |title=Aaron Jackson también deja el Bilbao Basket |trans-title=Aaron Jackson also leaves Bilbao |language=es |work=[[El Correo]] |location=Bilbao |date=May 23, 2022 |accessdate=April 18, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130520055809/http://bilbaobasket.elcorreo.com/noticias/2012-05-23/aaron-jackson-tambien-deja-201205231455.html |archive-date=May 20, 2013}} ===CSKA Moscow (2012–2017)=== On June 19, 2012, Jackson joined former opponents CSKA Moscow, penning a 3-year deal with perennial Russian champions, hours after they announced the return of former coach [[Ettore Messina]] who coached Real Madrid in 2010–11. He chose to sign with them instead of having another go at the NBA summer league.[http://www.imgacademy.com/latest-headlines/2012-07-26/getting-knowformer-duquesne-star-and-european-basketball-standout-aaron "Getting to Know...Former Duquesne Star and European Basketball Standout Aaron Jackson."], ''[[IMG Academy]]'', 26 June 2012. Retrieved on 11 April 2015. Transforming from a star player to a role player at the European giants, Jackson found it hard to adapt to the perfectionist Messina's coaching style and struggled with form and confidence, more so when the club brought [[Theo Papaloukas]] at his position. Little by little he improved, later playing a part in CSKA's championship victories in the [[2012–13 Russian Professional Basketball League|Russian League]] and the more competitive [[2012–13 VTB United League|VTB United League]], earning his first silverware, though they lost to [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] in the [[2012–13 Euroleague|EuroLeague]] semifinals, as the preceding year in the final. Despite offers from other EuroLeague teams of a starting place on their roster he stayed put and was also confirmed by CSKA who had an option to terminate his contract.[http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=12623&lang=en "Jackson, Micov and Zozulin stay in CSKA."], ''[[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]'', 12 June 2013. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. At the beginning of the season Jackson found himself behind [[Miloš Teodosić]] and newly arrived [[Jeremy Pargo]] in the rotation, playing most of his minutes as a [[shooting guard]], for instance in the October [[NBA versus Euroleague games#2010s|exhibition game]] against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].[http://www.nba.com/games/20131007/MOSMIN/gameinfo.html#nbaGIboxscore "Minnesota Timberwolves – CSKA Mosvow (Boxscore)."], ''[[NBA]]'', Minneapolis, 7 October 2013. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. When Teodosić got injured in March 2014, Jackson was chosen to replace him,[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/135690/playoffs-series-analysis-cska-moscow-vs-panathinaikos-athens "Playoffs series analysis: CSKA Moscow vs. Panathinaikos Athens."], ''[[EuroLeague]]'', 15 April 2014. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. playing nearly 31 minutes per game in the EuroLeague [[2013–14 Euroleague Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] against [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]], though he finished with only 5.4 in PIR.[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=003413&seasoncode=E2013 "Jackson, Aaron: 2013–14 Statistics."], ''[[EuroLeague]]''. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. Teodosić reclaimed his place after healing and Jackson barely featured in the [[2014 Euroleague Final Four#CSKA Moscow vs. Maccabi Tel Aviv|semi-final]] meltdown loss to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]], he even picked up a knee injury late in the game,[http://www.cskabasket.com/news/?id=13449&lang=en "Aaron Jackson out for season."], ''[[PBC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]]'', 17 May 2013. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. which kept him out of the Red Army club's consolation come from behind title in the VTB United League.[http://en.lokobasket.com/news/3674678.html "Lokomotiv Kuban – CSKA. Preview."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304134103/http://en.lokobasket.com/news/3674678.html |date=2016-03-04 }}, ''[[BC Lokomotiv–Kuban Krasnodar|Lokomotiv Kuban]]'', 21 May 2014. Retrieved on 13 April 2015. Having again seen the club fail in their EuroLeague title quest, the management decided to change the team roster, replacing Messina with [[Dimitrios Itoudis]] and [[Nando de Colo]] was signed to be the team's new shooting guard, with Teodosić's contract extended.[http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-adjustment.htm "CSKA. Adjustment."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526031013/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/cska-adjustment.htm |date=2015-05-26 }}, ''[[VTB United League]]'', 25 September 2014. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. This left one of Jackson or Pargo as surplus to requirements, amidst interest from [[Valencia BC|Valencia]][http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20140719/baloncesto/otros/el-valencia-basket-pendiente-de-la-posible-salida-de-aaron-jackson-del-cska_54412279121.html "Valencia Basket, waiting on the possible exit of Aaron Jackson from CSKA."], ''[[El Mundo Deportivo (newspaper)]]'', Valencia, 19 July 2014. Retrieved on 13 April 2015.{{in lang|es}} and due to the cost of Pargo's contract, coach Itoudis voted for JacksonLevov, Anton. [http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2013/9/29.asp "Eurobasket news report (7/14/2014) – CSKA looks to offload Aaron Jackson or Jeremy Pargo."], ''[[Eurobasket.com]]'', 14 July 2014. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. and it was Pargo that was released. Jackson repaid that faith with a strong start to the 2014–15 season, including a stretch in December that saw him nominated for the VTB United League Monthly Award.[http://www.vtb-league.com/en/mvpmonth/mvp-december-2014.htm "December MVP."] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150106184032/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/mvpmonth/mvp-december-2014.htm |date=2015-01-06 }}, ''[[VTB United League]]'', 29 December 2014. Retrieved on 14 April 2015. He also had a decisive contribution in the EuroLeague victory against [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes Istanbul]] in January, scoring 21 points without missing a single shot along with 4 rebounds and 4 assists to finish behind teammate De Colo in the Top 16 Round 3 MVP rankings.[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/5ovi5x5y7vcrxga9/top-16-round-3-bwin-mvp-nando-de-colo-cska-moscow "Top 16 Round 3 bwin MVP: Nando De Colo, CSKA Moscow."], ''[[Euroleague]]'', 17 January 2015. Retrieved on 14 April 2015. In a rotation system with De Colo, Teodosić and [[Sonny Weems]] occupying either the point guard, shooting guard or small forward positions, Jackson was often a substitute, however he had important contributions when called upon, for example in another EuroLeague [[2015 Euroleague Final Four#CSKA Moscow vs. Olympiacos|semi-final]] loss to Olympiacos, where his 7 steals broke the [[EuroLeague Final Four|Final Four]] single game record,[http://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/news/i/5ygh9cww6lkqjeke/aaron-jackson-sets-final-four-record-with-7-steals "Aaron Jackson sets Final Four record with 7 steals."], ''[[EuroLeague]]'', 15 May 2015. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. with 9 points, 3 assists for 1 turnover and 4 fouls drawn he was the third best rated player in that game.[http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=249&seasoncode=E2014 "2014–15 Final Four, Semifinal: CSKA Moscow – Olympiacos Piraeus (Boxscore)."], ''[[Euroleague]]'', 15 May 2015. Retrieved on 22 May 2015. Jackson was credited as "one of CSKA's best players down the stretch" in the VTB United League playoffs, posting 8.7 points, 6.1 assists and 1.8 steals per game whilst playing more minutes (24.5) and being seen as more effective than fellow guards De Colo and Teodosić. The Moscow club finished unbeaten in the playoffs to win the [[2014–15 VTB United League]] as Jackson contributed 12 points and 8 assists in the final series Game 3 against [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].{{cite web|url=http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/dazzling-dozen-12-playoff-stars.htm |title=Dazzling dozen. 12 playoff stars |date=10 June 2015 |website=[[VTB United League]] |access-date=20 June 2015 CSKA Moscow.{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/659hte83ne6nhl9s |title=CSKA keeps playmaker Jackson |author= |date=19 June 2015 |website=[[EuroLeague]] |access-date=20 June 2015}} Jackson to a two-year deal|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/asia/240188/beijing-ducks-sign-aaron-jackson-to-a-two-year-deal.html|access-date=July 6, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=July 6, 2017|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} ===Houston Rockets (2018)=== Near the end of the [[2017–18 NBA season]], Jackson would sign a contract with the [[Houston Rockets]], replacing the position previously [https://web.archive.org/web/20090727150532/http://blogs.courant.com/uconn_mens_basketball/2009/07/aaron-jackson-and-aj-price.html "Aaron Jackson and A.J.Price."], ''[[Hartford Courant]]'', 23 July 2009. Jackson is considered to be a high energy player with solid athleticism and an unselfish style.[http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/aaron_jackson_2009.html "Prospect Interview: Aaron Jackson."], ''[[Indiana Pacers]]''. Retrieved on 14 April 2015. On offense he is a creative [[Slasher (basketball)|slasher]], who is at his best while pushing the ball at a fast pace in transition.Givony, Jonathan. [http://www.draftexpress.com/article/NCAA-Weekly-Performers-22409-3119/ "NCAA Weekly Performers, 2/24/09."], ''DraftExpress (commercial website)'', 24 February 2009. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. He is adept at getting to the basket to finish around the rim, with either hand, and often in acrobatic fashion, even through contact. He can also "quarterback" his team's offense when called upon, using basketball IQ to great effect.Whelan, Joey. [http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Aaron-Jackson-El-Hombre-del-ACB-Playoff-3744/ "Aaron Jackson: El Hombre del ACB Playoff."], ''DraftExpress (commercial website)'', 8 June 2011. Retrieved on 20 May 2015. On defense he's a dynamic perimeter defender, who isn't afraid to play aggressively. At CSKA, he was used for lock-down individual defense, to try to force a turnover from the opponent. He is athletic, competitive, and not afraid of contact.[http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/10-contenders-for-defensive-player-of-the-year.htm "10 contenders for Defensive Player of the Year"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150416155739/http://www.vtb-league.com/en/news/10-contenders-for-defensive-player-of-the-year.htm |date=2015-04-16 }}, ''[[VTB United League]]'', 31 March 2015. It was noted in 2009, that he could improve his decision-making skills, ball-handling, mid-range jump shot, and defensive fundamentals, whilst highlighting his effort and potential. His work ethic and motivation, along with expert coachingPick, David. [http://www.eurobasket.com/reports/2013/9/29.asp "Eurobasket news report (9/29/2013) – Trust. With Ettore Messina, Aaron Jackson and JR Holden."], ''[[Eurobasket.com]]'', 26 June 2012. Retrieved on 21 May 2015. helped him correct some of those shortcomings, as evidenced by his defensive progress, which was formerly a weakness. It improved so much that he was named one of the top 10 defenders in the [[VTB United League]], in 2015. [http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=75171 "Ajax: the fastest guy of the Liga."], ''[[Liga ACB]]'', 5 April 2011. Retrieved on 15 April 2015.{{in lang|es}} ===Duquesne shooting=== On September 17, 2006, Jackson and four other [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]] teammates [[Sam Ashaolu]], Stuart Baldonado, [[Shawn James (basketball)|Shawn James]] and Kojo Mensah were the victims of an unprovoked shooting on the university's Pittsburgh campus. Ashaolu was shot in the head and neck, Mensah in the shoulder and arm, Baldonado through his back into his elbow, James in his left foot whilst Jackson was only grazed on the wrist by a bullet. He later carried the injured Baldonado to his car and drove him to hospital.Harlan, Chico. [https://www.post-gazette.com/local/2007/02/25/Basketball-A-season-in-chaos/stories/200702250258 "Basketball: A season in chaos."]''[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]]'', 25 February 2005. Retrieved on 27 March 2015. The two shooters, William B. Holmes II and Derek Lee pleaded guilty and were sentenced to respectively up to 40 years and up to 14 years in prison, for having helped them enter a student dance whilst armed, former university student Brittany Jones was sentenced to two years of probation. An altercation started during the dance after a female acquaintance of the shooters flirted with one of the Duquesne players, the players walked away but later re-encountered the two men, who started shooting at them.[http://www.wtae.com/sports/Judge-tosses-lawsuits-by-Duquesne-basketball-players-who-were-shot-on-campus/19543980 "Judge tosses lawsuits by Duquesne basketball players who were shot on campus."]''[[WTAE-TV]]'', Pittsburgh, 1 April 2013. Retrieved on 18 March 2015. Jackson was able to play the next season, the only one of the four to do so, he was a roommate and friend of Ashaolu and helped him through his rehabilitation, even having to carry him to his car and drive him to hospital after a seizure. Though Ashaolu was never able to play basketball again, he graduated in 2009 along with Jackson who earned a psychology degree.Katz, Andy. [https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?id=4750082 "One dream denied, one fulfilled."]''[[ESPN]]'', Pittsburgh, 17 December 2009.
